narrative: A couple in their late forties and fifties left Aleppo with their three adult children, including their youngest, who has developmental disabilities and needed urgent medical care. They left Syria two months before they were interviewed, and reached the Greek island of Lesbos the night before, speaking over each other as couples do. They had had a good life in Aleppo, but the war meant no hospitals, no doctors, no electricity, no water - only bombs, attacks and groups fighting each other. Their son needed care that was no longer available, and in Aleppo people died in the street; an attack could come at any moment. The husband was abashed that he had broken the law to reach Greece, saying it was the first time in his life he had done anything illegal, and that he had been forced to make the journey because he did not want to put his family in danger. At the time of the interview they had reached Lesbos, still in transit and far from the safety they were seeking.
